insights.claim: The orchestrator explicitly selects ring as its TLS crypto provider across all Rust TLS dependencies, which prevents FIPS compliance at the application level without a crypto backend change or TLS proxy delegation.
insights.reasoning: All TLS crate dependencies in Cargo.toml explicitly enable the ring feature rather than aws-lc-rs or a FIPS-capable provider. The Cargo.lock confirms ring is resolved as the crypto backend. ring is not FIPS-validated, so the application TLS stack cannot satisfy FIPS requirements without either changing the feature flags to aws-lc-rs with FIPS mode or delegating TLS termination to a FIPS-capable sidecar or gateway.

insights.claim: The orchestrator uses a passthrough authentication model where it forwards configured headers to downstream services without performing its own token validation, relying on the platform or downstream services for actual authentication enforcement.
insights.reasoning: The filter_headers function forwards a configurable set of headers from incoming requests to downstream services without validating token contents. The optional X-Forwarded-Access-Token rewrite converts platform-injected tokens into standard Bearer authorization headers. This passthrough pattern means the orchestrator itself does not enforce authentication policies; enforcement is delegated to the downstream detector, chunker, and generation services or to platform-level ingress controls.
